finding: In al-Kahf, the repeated arrival frame حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ opens three Dhu al-Qarnayn stations, each followed by a وَجَدَ discovery; 18:86 is the first where the sequence brings him to a people subject to his rule.

evidence.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍۢ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًۭا
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ مَطْلِعَ ٱلشَّمْسِ وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍۢ لَّمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُم مِّن دُونِهَا سِتْرًۭا
حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ بَيْنَ ٱلسَّدَّيْنِ وَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمَا قَوْمًۭا لَّا يَكَادُونَ يَفْقَهُونَ قَوْلًۭا

activation: The focus has بَلَغَ followed by two وَجَدَ clauses; 18:90 and 18:93 reuse the arrival-and-discovery sequence at the next stations.
limits: The repeated frame establishes narrative staging, not exact cardinal coordinates, a mapped route, or identity among the three peoples.

finding: مَغْرِبَ places the first expedition at the sun’s setting pole, while the next names مَطْلِعَ ٱلشَّمْسِ; 2:115 pairs east and west in a broad directional frame. The western stop therefore belongs to an east-and-west horizon sequence, with the wider Quranic usage in view.

evidence.ar: وَلِلَّهِ ٱلْمَشْرِقُ وَٱلْمَغْرِبُ ۚ فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا۟ فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ ٱللَّهِ

activation: The focus names مَغْرِبَ ٱلشَّمْسِ, and the next journey names مَطْلِعَ ٱلشَّمْسِ, while 2:115 supplies the explicit east-and-west pairing.
limits: This directional pattern does not specify the route’s geography or establish that these stops exhaust the earth.

finding: Across Surah 18, the sun marks different conditions of human exposure: it turns away from the cave sleepers, is seen setting by a people at the western stop, and rises upon a people with no screen from it. The focus becomes the middle scene in a sequence linking solar setting to how people inhabit their surroundings.

evidence.ar: وَتَرَى ٱلشَّمْسَ إِذَا طَلَعَت تَّزَٰوَرُ عَن كَهْفِهِمْ ذَاتَ ٱلْيَمِينِ وَإِذَا غَرَبَت تَّقْرِضُهُمْ ذَاتَ ٱلشِّمَالِ وَهُمْ فِى فَجْوَةٍۢ مِّنْهُ
وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍۢ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًۭا
وَجَدَهَا تَطْلُعُ عَلَىٰ قَوْمٍۢ لَّمْ نَجْعَل لَّهُم مِّن دُونِهَا سِتْرًۭا

activation: The focus joins the sun’s setting to a nearby human group, between the cave scene and the next account of a people exposed to sunrise.
limits: The juxtaposition does not establish that the communities share one environment or have equal protection from the sun.

finding: In the surah, وَجَدَ introduces consequential encounters: Moses and his companion find a servant at 18:65 and a wall at 18:77. In the focus, its doubled use first predicates the sun’s state, then identifies nearby people, pivoting from observation to a decision about how to treat them.

evidence.ar: فَوَجَدَا فِيهَا جِدَارًۭا يُرِيدُ أَن يَنقَضَّ فَأَقَامَهُۥ
وَجَدَهَا تَغْرُبُ فِى عَيْنٍ حَمِئَةٍۢ وَوَجَدَ عِندَهَا قَوْمًۭا

activation: The focus repeats وَجَدَ with a different object and construction, then moves directly into divine speech setting out two options for the people.
limits: The verb itself does not encode instruction or governance; those consequences depend on each scene and what is found.

finding: The Quranic root appears in water forms such as عَيْن in the focus and مَّعِين for water in 67:30, as well as the ocular description عِين in 37:48. Since the focus places the sun’s perceived setting فِي عَيْنٍ, an eye or aperture image at the horizon may accompany the spring image.
missing: A lexicon entry establishing both eye and spring senses for this singular form, or a Quranic parallel joining eye or aperture imagery to a spring at the horizon, could decide whether the visual echo is active. The focus construction favors a muddy spring, and the cited water and ocular examples use distinct forms.
